track.name: Drone technology
track.blurb: A calm, practical start to understanding how a multirotor flies.

apply.title: Sketch a four-motor flight
apply.detail: Draw four rotors. Add arrows for lift, a forward tilt, and a turn. Label what changes for each move.

units.title: Lift and thrust
lookFor: Air pushes the craft upward in response.
Tilting redirects part of that force sideways.
units.explanation: A rotor accelerates air down. The reaction pushes the craft up. When the craft tilts, some of that push points sideways, so it moves across the air.
units.videoTodo: A short video for this unit is coming soon. The points above and the check below work without it.

check.q: What does a rotor mainly push to make lift?
check.why: The rotor pushes air down, and the reaction pushes the craft up.

check.q: What makes a multirotor move forward?
options: Tilting so part of thrust points forward
check.why: A forward tilt redirects part of the total thrust.

check.q: What happens if total lift is less than weight?
check.why: The upward force cannot balance the craft's weight.

cards: What do rotors push to make lift?
Air downward; the reaction pushes the craft up.
How does a multirotor move sideways?
It tilts, redirecting part of its thrust sideways.
If lift falls below weight, what happens?
The craft descends.

units.title: Four motors and three turns
lookFor: Opposite rotors spin in matching directions.
Roll tilts left or right; pitch tilts forward or back.
Yaw rotates the nose around a vertical axis.
units.explanation: A flight controller changes motor speeds in pairs. Uneven lift tilts the craft for roll or pitch. Changing the balance of rotor torque rotates it in yaw.
units.videoTodo: A short video for this unit is coming soon. The points above and the check below work without it.

check.q: Which motion tips the craft left or right?
Which motion turns the nose without requiring forward travel?
check.why: Yaw turns around the vertical axis.

check.q: How can the controller create a tilt?
check.why: Different speeds create different lift at each side.

cards: What is roll?
Tilting the craft left or right.
What is pitch?
Tilting the craft forward or back.
What is yaw?
Turning the nose around the vertical axis.

units.title: Batteries and flight time
lookFor: Motors draw energy from the battery.
More lift generally uses more power.
A heavier battery also raises the lift required.
units.explanation: Flight time depends on usable battery energy and how quickly the craft spends it. Carrying more battery can help, but its extra weight also costs energy.
units.videoTodo: A short video for this unit is coming soon. The points above and the check below work without it.

check.q: What draws much of a multirotor's electrical energy?
check.why: The motors do the main work of moving air.

check.q: Why might a larger battery add less flight time than expected?
options: Its extra mass needs more lift
check.why: Extra mass makes the motors work harder.

check.q: Which change usually uses more power?
check.why: More lift generally takes more motor power.

cards: What is flight time mainly balancing?
Usable battery energy against the rate of power use.
Why does battery weight matter?
More mass requires more lift and energy.
What usually happens to power use when more lift is demanded?
It rises.

units.title: IMU, GPS, and barometer
lookFor: The IMU senses rotation and acceleration.
GPS estimates position outdoors when signals are available.
A barometer senses air pressure to help estimate altitude changes.
units.explanation: The controller combines different sensor clues. The IMU reacts quickly to motion; GPS gives a slower position estimate; air pressure helps with height changes. None is a perfect reading alone.
units.videoTodo: A short video for this unit is coming soon. The points above and the check below work without it.

check.q: Which sensor helps detect quick rotation?
check.why: The IMU includes a gyroscope for rotation.

check.q: What does GPS mainly help estimate?
check.why: GPS offers a position estimate when signals are available.

check.q: What does a barometer measure directly?
check.why: Pressure changes help estimate changes in height.

cards: What does an IMU help sense?
Rotation and acceleration.
What does GPS help estimate?
Position when signals are available.
What does a barometer measure?
Air pressure, which helps estimate altitude changes.
